header.running_head: The fervour that Rasulullaah ﷺ and the Sahabah (RA) had to Spend in the Path of Allaah

blocks.arabic_text: وَيُطْعِمُوْنَ الطَّعَامَ عَلٰى حُبِّهٖ مِسْكِيْنًا وَّيَتِيْمًا وَّاَسِيْرًا
blocks.text: Out of love for Allaah, they feed the poor, the orphan and the captive. [^1]

blocks.arabic_text: وَالَّذِيْنَ فِيْٓ اَمْوَالِهِمْ حَقٌّ مَّعْلُوْمٌ لِّلسَّآئِلِ وَالْمَحْرُوْمِ
blocks.text: And (they are those) who have a stipulated right (have fixed a share) in their wealth for the beggar and the destitute. [^2]"
Hadhrat Abu Dharr (RA) then continued quoting several similar verses from the Qur'aan.[^3]
The Statement of Hadhrat Umar (RA) Concerning how Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) was Always in the lead when it Came to Spending in Charity

Hadhrat Umar (RA) says, "Rasulullaah ﷺ once instructed us to spend in charity at a time when I happened to have a considerable sum of wealth with me. I therefore said to myself, 'If there be any day when I shall beat Abu Bakr (RA) (at spending in the path of Allaah), it shall be this day.' I then brought half of all my wealth. Rasulullaah ﷺ asked, 'What have you left for your family?' 'I have left something for them,' I responded. Rasulullaah ﷺ repeated, 'What have you left for them?' I said, 'I have left with them as much as I have brought.' Abu Bakr (RA) then arrived with everything that he possessed. When Rasulullaah ﷺ asked him what he had left for his family, he replied, 'I have left (the pleasure of) Allaah and His Rasool ﷺ for them.' It was then that I declared that I will never be able to beat him at anything afterwards." [^4]
The Incident of Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) and another Man in this Regard

Hadhrat Hasan narrates that a man once said to Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA), "You wealthy people have far superseded us (poor people) on doing good because you are able to give Sadaqah, free slaves, perform Hajj and spend in the path of Allaah." Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) asked, "Do you envy us?" "We certainly do," the man responded. Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) then said, "I swear by Allaah that a single Dirham that a person donates while he is in financial difficulty is better than ten thousand Dirhams given when there is still so much more left." [^5]

blocks.text: Hadhrat Ubaydullaah bin Muhammad bin Aa'isha narrates that when a beggar came to the Ameerul Mu'mineen Hadhrat Ali (RA), he said to (his son) Hadhrat
Bayhaqi, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.3 Pg.310).
Abu Dawood, Tirmidhi, Daarmi, Haakim, Bayhaqi, Abu Nu'aym in his Hilya and others, as quoted in Muntakhab Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.4 Pg.347).
